qa_pairs.question: When does the standard add/drop period end for Fall 2026?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The standard add/drop period for Fall 2026 ends at 17:00 on August 28.

qa_pairs.question: How much is undergraduate tuition per credit for 2026-2027, and how much is the student-services fee in Fall?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Undergraduate tuition is USD 420 per registered credit for the 2026-2027 academic year, and the student-services fee is USD 180 in Fall.

qa_pairs.question: What is the minimum attendance expectation, and may a course syllabus set a different threshold?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance. A syllabus may set a higher threshold when required by accreditation, laboratory safety, or clinical practice, but it may not set a lower one.

contexts.text: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance. A course syllabus may set a higher threshold when required by accreditation, laboratory safety, or clinical practice, but it may not set a lower threshold.

qa_pairs.question: What academic requirements make an undergraduate eligible to graduate?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An undergraduate is academically eligible to graduate after completing at least 120 applicable credits, all programme-required courses, the capstone requirement, and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.00.

contexts.text: An undergraduate student is academically eligible to graduate after completing at least 120 applicable credits, all programme-required courses, the capstone requirement, and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.00.

qa_pairs.question: Is multi-factor authentication required for the student portal, and will staff ever ask for my password?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Multi-factor authentication is required for the portal, and staff will never request a password or one-time authentication code.

qa_pairs.question: What approvals and payment does a late add require, and is the late-add fee refundable?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval; failing to pay on time cancels the late add. The late-add fee is non-refundable unless the university cancels the course or confirms an administrative error.

contexts.text: A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Failure to pay on time cancels the late add.
The late-add fee is non-refundable unless the university cancels the course or confirms an administrative error.

qa_pairs.question: What must a Merit Scholarship recipient achieve to renew the award, and where and within what deadline is a scholarship decision appealed?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: To renew, the recipient must complete at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, earn a term GPA of at least 3.30, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, and have no active serious-conduct sanction. A scholarship decision may be appealed within ten business days, and the appeal goes to the Financial Aid Review Committee.

contexts.text: To renew, a recipient must complete at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, earn a term GPA of at least 3.30, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, and have no active serious-conduct sanction.
Scholarship decisions use the same ten-business-day filing window but go to the Financial Aid Review Committee.

qa_pairs.question: A Fall 2026 student drops one course on September 1 and stays enrolled in the rest. How much of that course's tuition is reversed?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: September 1 is after the end of standard add/drop on August 28 but on or before the September 4 census date, so 50% of that course's tuition is reversed.

contexts.text: the standard add/drop period ends at 17:00 on August 28. The census date is September 4.
For a course dropped by the end of standard add/drop, 100% of that course's tuition is reversed. From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% is reversed.

qa_pairs.question: What steps and deadlines apply to a formal grade appeal, and is disagreeing with the instructor's academic judgement a permitted ground?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published, then file a formal grade appeal within ten business days after publication identifying at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.

contexts.text: The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.
A disagreement about academic judgement is handled first with the instructor.

qa_pairs.question: What must a student do to request a standard leave of absence and to return from it, and what happens to a Merit Scholarship during an approved medical leave?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The student must submit the request before the census date, explain the reason, provide any required documentation, and obtain programme approval; to return, they submit a return notice at least 20 calendar days before regular registration closes. An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity.

contexts.text: The student must submit the request before the census date, explain the reason, provide any required documentation, and obtain programme approval.
To return from approved leave, a student submits a return notice at least 20 calendar days before regular registration closes.
An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity.

qa_pairs.question: How does a waitlist offer work when a seat opens, and can a student with an unpaid balance and a financial hold take that seat?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: When a seat opens, the first eligible student receives a 24-hour offer, and if it expires the next eligible student is contacted. Waitlist position does not override prerequisite, time-conflict, or hold rules, and a financial hold from an unpaid balance blocks new registration, so the student cannot take the seat until the hold is resolved.

contexts.text: When a seat opens, the first eligible student receives a 24-hour offer. If the offer expires, the next eligible student is contacted. Waitlist position does not override prerequisite, time-conflict, or hold rules.
An unpaid balance after the grace period receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold. The hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance.

qa_pairs.question: How many internship hours are required, may they be split across placements, and when should a degree audit be requested?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Programmes with an internship requirement need at least 240 verified hours, and the student must have an approved placement agreement and workplace supervisor before starting because hours completed before approval do not normally count. The hours may be split across two approved placements, but each placement requires its own agreement. A degree audit should be requested two regular terms before the intended graduation term.

contexts.text: Programmes with an internship requirement require at least 240 verified hours. Before starting, the student must have an approved placement agreement and workplace supervisor. Hours completed before approval do not normally count.
A student may split the hours across two approved placements, but each placement requires its own agreement.
Students should request a degree audit two regular terms before the intended graduation term.

qa_pairs.question: A student first discussed a late add with the instructor in July 2026 but submitted the request on August 20, 2026. Which registration policy version applies, what does it cost, and how late may the add be made?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Version 2.0 applies because the late-add request was made on or after August 1, 2026, even though it was first discussed in July. Under version 2.0 the late-add window runs from the end of standard add/drop through the census date and the fee is USD 40 per course, not the USD 25 charged under version 1.0.

contexts.text: Registration Policy version 1.0, effective before August 1, 2026, allowed late adds for seven calendar days after standard add/drop and charged USD 25. Version 2.0, effective August 1, 2026, allows late adds only through census and charges USD 40 per course. A late-add request made on or after August 1, 2026 follows version 2.0 even if the student first discussed the request in July.
Version 2.0 introduces a late-add window from the end of standard add/drop through the census date.

qa_pairs.question: A Merit Scholarship recipient is already on probation after a failed Fall review. In Spring they withdraw from a course after the census date and finish with only 9 completed graded credits. What happens to the award?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The award ends beginning with the next term. The withdrawal after census still counts as attempted credit but not completed credit, so the student finishes Spring below the 12 graded Northstar credits required for renewal and fails the review. Because the Fall review had already failed, this is a second consecutive failed review, which ends the award rather than granting another probation term.

contexts.text: To renew, a recipient must complete at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, earn a term GPA of at least 3.30, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, and have no active serious-conduct sanction.

A first failure to meet one academic renewal requirement normally produces one term of scholarship probation rather than immediate loss. During probation, the award remains active. A second consecutive failed review ends the award beginning with the next term.
A withdrawal after census still counts as attempted credit but not completed credit and may cause failure at the end-of-term review.

qa_pairs.question: A student's last documented participation was March 2 because of a documented illness, and they file for medical leave on April 20. Can the retroactive request still be considered, and what tuition outcome follows an approved medical withdrawal?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: April 20 is more than 30 calendar days after the last documented participation on March 2, so the request is past the normal retroactive filing window and requires evidence that the condition also prevented filing during that 30-day period. If an approved medical withdrawal follows, the student may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study calculated from the last documented date of participation; it is not a cash refund.

contexts.text: Medical leave may be approved retroactively when a documented condition prevented timely submission. A retroactive request must normally be filed within 30 calendar days after the student's last documented participation. Later requests require evidence that the condition also prevented filing during that 30-day period.
An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation. It is not a cash refund

qa_pairs.question: A student holding an `I` incomplete grade submitted no work by the end of the next regular term and now wants to challenge the resulting grade. What grade results, and what escalation exists after the chair's review?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Because no grade was submitted by the default deadline at the end of the next regular term, the `I` converts to `F` unless an approved extension exists. A grade appeal is reviewed first by the department chair, and the chair's outcome may be appealed to the Academic Review Panel within five business days only when there is new material evidence or a documented procedural error in the first review; the Panel's decision is final within the university process.

contexts.text: The default deadline is the end of the next regular term. If no grade is submitted by that deadline, the `I` converts to `F` unless an approved extension exists.

The department chair reviews a grade appeal first. A student may appeal the chair's outcome to the Academic Review Panel within five business days only when there is new material evidence or a documented procedural error in the first review. The Panel's decision is final within the university process.

qa_pairs.question: A student completed every course requirement, walked at commencement, but still has an unpaid balance. Has the degree been conferred, and can they receive the final transcript?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No. Participation in commencement is ceremonial and is not proof that a degree has been conferred, and the transcript will not show the degree until every requirement and hold is cleared. Degree conferral requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds; the financial hold does not erase the completed academic requirements but blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until the balance is resolved.

contexts.text: Degree conferral also requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds. A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until resolved

Participation in a commencement ceremony is ceremonial and is not proof that a degree has been conferred. Students with no more than six credits remaining may request permission to participate early, but the transcript will not show the degree until every requirement and hold is cleared.

The Northstar Student Services Assistant provides general information from the official documents in this corpus.

qa_pairs.question: Since Northstar gives every student a full cash refund for any course withdrawn after the census date, how do I claim the refund for the course I withdrew from last week?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The premise is incorrect, so there is no such refund to claim. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal. The only related exception is an approved medical withdrawal, which may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study calculated from the last documented date of participation and is not a cash refund. The assistant should state what the documents say and direct the student to the responsible office rather than confirm the premise.

contexts.text: After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal.
An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation. It is not a cash refund

The assistant must not invent a policy when the documents do not contain an answer. If information is missing or two current documents appear inconsistent, it should say what is known, identify the uncertainty, and direct the student to the responsible office.
